name: Sexual offenses, consent, and privacy
description: Legal constructs addressing non-consensual sexual acts, exploitation of incapacity, and privacy-related sexual wrongs—areas where modern law foregrounds autonomy and harm, while historical and religious moral language often emphasized lust and chastity.
foundationStrengthRationale: Rapid legal and social change around consent, age, and digital harms; high contestation.

pros.claim: Centers consent and protection of vulnerable persons in ways many frameworks converge on.
pros.evidence: International human-rights instruments and national reforms increasingly align on consent-centric models.

cons.claim: Moral-theological 'lust' and legal 'lack of consent' are not coextensive; marriage law, obscenity, and morals offenses show persistent divergence.
cons.evidence: Jurisdictions differ on criminalization of adult consensual conduct and on sex work.
